page.title: Marbella Full Moon Cruise with Champagne: Night Magic

data.meta_description: Experience a magical Marbella full moon cruise with champagne. Book a private boat from Puerto Banús, sip cava under the moonlight, and enjoy the Costa del Sol night. Reserve now!
data.summary: A Marbella full moon cruise with champagne combines luxury, romance, and the stunning Costa del Sol coastline. Depart from Puerto Banús at sunset, toast with cava, and watch the moon rise over the Mediterranean.
key_facts: Best time: sunset to moonrise (approx. 4-hour charter)
Champagne/cava, soft drinks, beer, and snacks included
Licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and 21% IVA included
Private charter for up to 12 guests (depending on boat)
Popular boats: Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) or Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h with jet ski)

faq.q: What is included in a Marbella full moon cruise with champagne?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Champagne or cava is served as part of the drinks package, so you can toast the moonrise without extra cost.

faq.q: Which boats are best for a full moon cruise in Marbella?
faq.a: The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are popular for intimate groups, starting at €749 for 2 hours. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers a flybridge and jet ski, from €4,719 for 4 hours. All depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: How long should a full moon cruise last?
faq.a: A 2-hour charter is enough for a sunset toast and moonrise views. For a more relaxed experience, 4 hours lets you cruise to Cabopino or Estepona, anchor for a swim, and watch the moon climb higher. Most guests book 3–4 hours.

faq.q: Can we swim during the full moon cruise?
faq.a: Yes, if the sea conditions allow. Many boats have a swim platform and ladder. Popular anchor spots include Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. Night swimming under the full moon is magical, but always follow the skipper's safety instructions.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a full moon cruise in Marbella?
faq.a: May to October offers warm evenings (20–28°C) and calm seas. June, July, and August have the most consistent weather. Check the lunar calendar for the exact full moon date; sunset and moonrise align beautifully in summer.

faq.q: How do I book a full moon cruise in Marbella?
faq.a: You can book directly via our website or WhatsApp. Choose your boat, date, and duration. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), pricing is fixed online. For larger yachts, request a quote. All bookings include free cancellation up to 48 hours.

faq.q: What should I bring on a full moon cruise?
faq.a: Bring a light jacket or sweater (sea breeze can be cool at night), sunglasses, sunscreen, a camera, and swimwear if you plan to swim. The boat provides towels, drinks, and snacks. No need to bring extra food or alcohol.

data.body_html:
There is something undeniably magical about watching the full moon rise over the Mediterranean while sipping chilled champagne on a private yacht. A Marbella full moon cruise with champagne is the perfect way to celebrate a special occasion, surprise a partner, or simply indulge in the Costa del Sol's night beauty. Departing from glamorous Puerto Banús, you can toast the moonrise with cava, cruise past the illuminated coastline, and enjoy the warm sea breeze under the stars.

Why a Full Moon Cruise in Marbella?

Marbella's microclimate delivers calm seas and clear skies more than 300 days a year. On a full moon night, the moonlight paints a silver path across the water, and the silhouette of La Concha mountain creates a stunning backdrop. A private charter means you have the boat to yourself—no crowds, no noise, just your group and the sea. The experience combines luxury, romance, and the freedom of the open water.

What You Get: Inclusions and Pricing

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). That means your Marbella full moon cruise with champagne is truly all-inclusive—no hidden extras. For a 2-hour sunset-to-moonrise trip, the Boat Rental Marbella fleet offers the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 from €749. For a longer 4-hour cruise with a jet ski, the Mangusta 80 is available from €4,719.

Best Boats for a Moonlit Night

For a cosy, intimate evening, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal. Both have comfortable salons, sunbathing areas, and a swim platform. If you prefer a larger deck and a flybridge for panoramic views, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) delivers space and speed. All boats depart from Puerto Banús, so you can step aboard minutes after arriving.

Suggested Itinerary: Sunset to Moonrise

Depart Puerto Banús 30 minutes before sunset. Head west towards Cabopino or east towards the Golden Mile. As the sun dips below the horizon, the sky turns orange and pink. Then, the full moon rises over the sea. Your skipper will find a quiet anchorage where you can enjoy a toast, take photos, and even take a night swim if conditions allow. Return to port under the moonlight—a memory that lasts a lifetime.

When to Book: Best Months and Moon Phases

The best season for a Marbella full moon cruise with champagne runs from May to October, when evening temperatures hover between 20°C and 28°C. June, July, and August offer the warmest waters and longest daylight hours. Check a lunar calendar for full moon dates; booking 2–3 weeks ahead is recommended, especially in peak summer. Weeknights are quieter and often more magical.
